title: Drone Panorama Editing: Batch RAW Adjustments, Horizon Work, and Sunset Color Grading

date.basis: embedded_creation_time; no independent transcript confirmation of the date.

summary: This instructional video guides a landscape photographer through post-processing a drone-based panorama composed of multiple RAW frames. The instructor demonstrates batch adjustments in Camera Raw, discusses horizon alignment when stitching drone-captured panels, and compares a traditional Transform workflow with a trapezoid/perspective approach. The workflow continues with puppet-warp-based refinement to preserve important foreground and sky while cropping, followed by sky augmentation via cloning and shadow/mid-tone dodging to enhance depth. Beams and dramatic sunset lighting are created with targeted dehaze and multi-pass color grading, culminating in iterative palette adjustments to achieve a cohesive, explosive sunset look while maintaining the form of the mountain and surrounding terrain.

sections.title: Import and batch exposure adjustments in Camera Raw
sections.description: The presenter imports multiple RAW files into Camera Raw, notes that drone cameras often auto-expose, and applies a uniform exposure adjustment across all frames by resetting to default and balancing shadows/blacks before selectively brightening individual files to achieve consistency.

sections.title: Horizon handling for drone panoramas and stitching
sections.description: The speaker explains how drone panoramas can produce a curved horizon due to gimbal movement, stresses placing the horizon near the middle of the frame to simplify later straightening, and suggests cropping the top or bottom to suit a desired composition.

sections.title: Perspective handling: trapezoid approach vs Transform
sections.description: The instructor expresses a preference for a trapezoid-like distortion over the standard Transform tool, arguing it better represents wide-angle perspective and preserving symmetry; steps include stretching and careful point-locking to avoid over-warping, with a note on crop-conscious decisions.

sections.title: Puppet Warp to preserve foreground while cropping
sections.description: The video demonstrates using Puppet Warp to subtly bend the image, keeping a key cloud/foreground area intact while ensuring the crop remains visually balanced; emphasizes that no sacrifice should be made to a desired portion of the frame.

sections.title: Sky cloning and dodge techniques for depth separation
sections.description: The editor clones sky areas and applies shadow/dodge to create a clearer separation between sky and mountains, adding depth and reducing distant textures that could flatten the scene.

sections.title: Beams, dehaze, and multi-pass color grading for sunset dynamics
sections.description: Beams are introduced using dehaze with carefully chosen parameters; the editor doubles down with iterative color grading, balancing warmth, mid-tones, highlights, and blues to craft a vivid sunset look, and notes parameter tuning is needed for very high-resolution imagery.

sections.title: Final color palette refinement and sunset storytelling
sections.description: The workflow culminates in additional color grading passes to reinforce the sunset palette, adjust whites/temperature, and apply sky-side color shifts to harmonize the overall image while considering how a too-textured sky can distract from the mountain form.
